analysis.title: France's debt crisis is no longer the story, contagion is
key_insights: France's 10-year yield is heading toward the 5% level and is trading above its 21-day moving average on a steep upward trendline, while remaining well below its 50-day moving average. The open question is whether it prints above 5% or pauses.

French OAT spreads versus Germany have widened sharply this month, while Italian and Greek spreads versus Germany have narrowed. Investors are treating France as an isolated sovereign problem, unlike the 2010-12 eurozone crisis. The note adds that France is part of the core, so nothing should be taken for granted.
The sell-off in European banks (SX7E) has coincided with the jump in the OAT-Bund spread. SX7E has fallen to its 200-day moving average, a level rarely tested since 2025.

Absolute Strategy Research (ASR) says the larger contagion risk may be foreign institutional holders of French government debt, not European banks. Foreign institutions own 57.5% of French government debt versus 35.9% of Italian government bonds. With French banks already under pressure, insurers and other institutional investors could be the next transmission channel.

France's public debt is approaching 110% of GDP and private-sector leverage is substantially higher than in the US and much of Europe. The government has little fiscal room and the private sector has little capacity to absorb more debt.
The euro's short-term negative trend remains intact. EURUSD is testing its 21-day moving average, the 100-day moving average has rolled over and slopes lower, and first major support is around 1.10.
The euro has paused its decline over the past few sessions despite French spreads continuing to widen. The note expects no more than a pause unless French stress eases.

sector_views.rationale: The note describes the latest sell-off as a surprise for a sector that had been a market favorite. SX7E is now at its 200-day moving average, and the note makes no overweight or underweight call.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The yield is on a steep uptrend above its 21-day moving average. A print above 5% would mark a key psychological breach and could deepen sovereign and bank stress.
High public debt limits the government's fiscal room, and elevated private leverage limits the private sector's ability to absorb more debt.

macro_indicators.indicator: Foreign institutional ownership of French government debt
macro_indicators.interpretation: High foreign ownership makes France more exposed to a pullback by non-domestic holders, such as insurers and other institutions.
First major support level for the euro as the short-term negative trend persists.

risk_factors: The French 10-year yield could break above 5%, extending sovereign stress.
The OAT-Bund spread continues to widen, pressuring European banks.
Foreign institutional holders of French debt, including insurers, could become a contagion channel.
France has limited fiscal and private-sector balance-sheet flexibility, with public debt near 110% of GDP.
A weaker euro if French stress persists, with 1.10 as first major support.
France is part of the eurozone core, so contagion to the rest of the region cannot be ruled out.

tension_points.bull_case: Contagion across the eurozone is contained. Italian and Greek spreads versus Germany have narrowed this month, and investors are treating France as an isolated sovereign problem, unlike the 2010-12 crisis.
tension_points.bear_case: France is part of the core, so nothing should be taken for granted. Foreign institutional holders (57.5% of French debt) and insurers could transmit stress, and European banks are already selling off as the OAT-Bund spread widens.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A French 10-year yield print above 5%, or Italian and Greek spreads versus Germany widening again.
